note: Joel B. Itzkowitz: Jews, Indians, Phylacteries: Jerome on Matthew 23:5. _Journal of Early Christian Studies_ 17 (2007) 563–572.

_vae autem vobis scribae_ – woe to you scribes (Douay Version). While the Vulgate’s _vae_ is treatening (with punishmen), the underlying Greek’s _ouai_ indicates a lamentation or grief (and may be rendered “alas”). – Hans Förster: Weherufe im Matthäusevangelium; in: Schmid/Fieger, pp. 117–119.
